tasks.title: A merchant with Create Role can grant the six finance permissions they do not hold
tasks.existing_status: NOT STARTED. S15-B row 8. The denylist has 13 names and omits the money-moving finance permissions.
acceptance: A merchant cannot grant a permission they do not themselves hold
The platform operator is unaffected
The denylist is not the only control (positive authorization, not a name blocklist)
tests: Negative: merchant with Create Role cannot mint a role carrying each of the six finance permissions
Positive: a merchant can still create an ordinary role within their own grants
tasks.compatibility: Merchant role management UI keeps working; only the permitted set narrows.
tasks.evidence: RolePolicy::grantPermission changed from a DENYLIST of 13 platform-operator names to POSITIVE AUTHORIZATION bounded by the tenant owner's own grant; the denylist is kept as defence in depth, consulted BEFORE the positive limb so a platform name stays refused even for a tenant that somehow held one. MEASURED AGAINST THE APPLICATION'S OWN SEEDER: Utility::addNewData seeds 200 permission rows, grants 181 to the merchant role and 29 to the operator role. Nineteen are outside a merchant's grant and the denylist covered only twelve; the seven it missed are the six money-moving finance permissions (whose rows exist and which NO SEEDED ROLE HOLDS -- Utility.php:2866-2876 records that as a deliberate owner privilege decision) plus Manage Email Template, which is operator-only and which a name-list fix would have missed again. REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION FIRST: three negatives fail and both positive controls pass against unfixed code. TESTS: tests/Feature/Security/FinancePermissionGrantTest.php -- 10 tests / 51 assertions, one case per finance permission, both call sites (store and update), both views, and three STAFF cases. SIX REMOVAL CHECKS, ALL BITE: RS1 denylist-only fails the negatives; RS2 denylist kept but the positive limb dropped STILL fails them (the measurement behind the third acceptance criterion -- the denylist is demonstrably not the control); RS3 dropping the operator exemption fails the operator control, having granted nothing; RS4 switching to ACTOR-bounding fails 'staff can grant what their merchant holds'; RS5 reverting to the denylist fails 'staff cannot grant what their merchant lacks'; RS6 removing the null-owner limb fails the orphan-staff case. GATES AT THE DELIVERED TREE: full Feature gate 2856 testcases, 2 declared failures, 17 declared skips, 0 errors, nothing undeclared, exit 0. Security + Tenancy 1571 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failures. Four CI guards exit 0. A PERFORMANCE REGRESSION I INTRODUCED AND THEN REMOVED, measured both ways: routing the role editor's per-permission check through the Gate cost 601 GateEvaluated events and 1,742 DB queries for one GET /roles/create on a 200-permission table, against 1 and 14 before the task -- 124x the queries on an AJAX modal merchants open routinely, and invisible to the suite because SecurityTestCase disables the Laratrust cache and the fixtures hold nine permissions. Fixed to 1 call / 18 queries / 0.069s by computing the grantable set once in the controller via RolePolicy::grantableNames() and testing membership in Blade. Both paths end in the same private per-name rule, so rules cannot drift; both now use EXACT membership rather than isAbleTo(), so MATCHING SEMANTICS cannot drift either -- which also closes a latent hazard the review raised, that Laratrust's Str::is treats the REQUESTED name as the pattern, so a permissions.name containing '*' would have cleared the ceiling. CORRECTIONS RECORDED: (1) THE OWNER-BOUNDING BRANCH HAD NEVER EXECUTED -- every principal was type admin or super admin, so tenantOwner()'s real path and the fail-closed limb were dead code and the central design decision had zero protection; three staff cases added. (2) The orphan-staff removal check was VACUOUS and PASSED with the control deleted: it read `if ($role !== null) { assertSame([], ...) }`, and removing the null limb makes a fatal -> 500 -> no role -> assertion skipped. It now asserts the response is not a 500 first, which separates 'fail closed' from 'crash'. (3) Two negatives lacked a per-case positive premise, so a fix refusing ALL grants would have satisfied them. (4) The role EDIT view was asserted by nothing. (5) isPlatformAdmin() was an exact === where CLAUDE.md and two other call sites normalise; it fails closed, but THIS TASK CHANGED WHAT THAT COSTS (a 'Super Admin' row went from granting 187 of 200 names to granting NOTHING, losing the operator the role editor), so it is now strtolower(trim(...)). (6) An analysis script of mine scraped quoted strings out of COMMENT PROSE and reported two permissions that do not exist; re-run comment-stripped. THREE PRE-EXISTING TESTS had fixtures encoding the denylist rule (RoleEscalationTest asserting an 'ordinary' permission stays grantable while granting the merchant nothing). Their fixtures now grant what production grants; NO ASSERTION WAS CHANGED, ADDED OR REMOVED -- verified by diff, the only removed line being $merchant -> $merchant->fresh(). DOCUMENTED, NOT CHANGED: tenantOwner() resolves to the OPERATOR for any user the operator created, so that principal's ceiling is the operator's grant minus the denylist -- strictly narrower than before, deliberately not special-cased. The coupling to RESERVED_NAMES is stated where it matters: staff at parity inherit Create Role + Edit User, the S13-b kit, contained only because a tenant role named 'admin' is refused. The duplicate $module_list block in create.blade.php is PRE-EXISTING, verified by diff against HEAD~2. RESIDUAL, recorded for the owner rather than chosen silently: staff can compose a role up to parity with their own merchant. Inside one tenant, strictly narrower than what this closes; actor-bounding would close it and would break merchant-to-staff delegation of role composition.

tasks.title: CategoryController destroys and rewrites another store's categories, product media, variants and live carts
tasks.existing_status: LIVE AND VERIFIED BY READING THE WHOLE CALL CHAIN in this session, raised out of the P1-INV-07 work. `DELETE /category/{id}` (Route::resource, routes/web.php:846) resolves `Category::find($id)` with no store predicate -- `Category` is absent from config/tenancy.php's scoped_models (grep -c "Category::class" -> 0) and the model registers no global scope. It then iterates `$mainCategory->product_details`, a plain hasMany(Product::class,'category_id') on the equally unscoped Product, and calls Product::productImageDelete() on each: that UNLINKS FROM DISK every product image, the cover image, the downloadable product and the preview video, and DELETES all product_images rows and all product_variants rows (and the stock they carry) -- neither model carries BelongsToStore and neither is allowlisted, so nothing narrows those two deletes. CORRECTION, made before acting on this row: the first draft also claimed the Cart delete at Product.php:659 destroys the victim's shoppers' baskets. IT DOES NOT in this request context -- App\Models\Cart carries BelongsToStore (Cart.php:17) AND is allowlisted (config/tenancy.php:298), so with the attacker's tenant resolved StoreScope compiles `AND store_id = <attacker>` and that delete matches no victim row. It holds only because a tenant resolves: StoreScope fails open on a null tenant by design, so the same call reached from a queued job, a scheduled command, or an operator with no users.current_store deletes EVERY store's cart rows for that product -- a second, narrower exposure on the same line, and the reason the fix belongs in destroy()'s own predicate rather than in trusting the scope. The only getCurrentStore() in the method is the child-category guard, which asks whether the VICTIM category's children belong to the ATTACKER's store; for a foreign category that is false, so the guard waves the deletion through and orphans the victim's child categories. More severe than the three sites P1-INV-07 closed, because disk unlinking is not recoverable from the application. SECOND LIVE SITE IN THE SAME CONTROLLER, read in the same pass: `update()` (:174, PUT category/{category}) is route-model-bound with `isAbleTo('Edit Product Category')` as its only authorization -- the exact shape P1-INV-01 closed on ProductController. It renames a foreign category, rewrites its slug, `parent_id` (so a foreign category can be reparented under one of the attacker's own), `trending` and `status`, and on an image upload calls `Utility::changeStorageLimit(\Auth::user()->creatorId(), $file_path)` which UNLINKS the victim's existing image from disk and debits the attacker's quota, then writes the replacement into `$dir = 'uploads/' . getCurrentStore()` -- the ATTACKER's upload directory. The other two resource methods were checked and are NOT defects: `edit($id)` already scopes with `Category::where('store_id', getCurrentStore())->find($id)`, and `show(Category $category)` has an empty body.

(6) MY OWN REMOVAL CHECK LEAKED A FILE into the tracked uploads/ tree, written by the HANDLER so the test's cleanup never saw it; the first fix cleaned up INLINE, which PHPUnit never reaches because it aborts at the first failed assertion -- moved to tearDown and re-verified. tasks.title: Unvalidated parent_id leaks every store's category names, and admits a tree cycle that fatals
tasks.existing_status: LIVE. Found by the adversarial review of P1-INV-08 and confirmed by reading the three files involved. P1-INV-08's guard cannot see it, because the row being written is the caller's OWN: categoryIsOutsideCurrentStore() correctly returns false. CategoryController writes parent_id straight from request input in both writers (:123 store, :281 update) with no `exists` rule and no store predicate -- the only validation rule in either is 'name' => 'required'. The value is rendered back through an UNSCOPED relation: Category::parent_category() is a plain belongsTo (Category.php:111-114) and CategoryDataTable renders optional($category->parent_category)->name (:58-60). So a merchant PUTs their own category with parent_id=N, loads /category, and the Parent Category column shows store B's category name -- incrementing N enumerates the platform's whole catalogue taxonomy, one name per request. The create/edit dropdown IS store-scoped, so the UI never offers a foreign id, but that is obscurity and the POST is hand-craftable. Second effect from the same missing rule: parent_id = own id, or any cycle, makes buildCategoryTree (helper.php:2538-2551, unconditional recursion with no visited-set) recurse until it fatals -- a 500 on the caller's own create and edit pages.

tasks.title: Deleting a category deletes every product in it by FK cascade, below the application
tasks.existing_status: FOUND BY A REGRESSION TEST FAILING, and it CORRECTS A CLAIM THIS PROJECT HAD ALREADY PUBLISHED. The P1-INV-08 test asserting that a foreign product sharing the caller's own category kept its rows went red: the row was gone. products.category_id is declared ON DELETE CASCADE against categories.id (create_products_table.php:55) and product_variants.product_id cascades again off products, so $category->delete() removes EVERY product row in the category and every variant under it, for every store, below the application -- no controller predicate can reach it. The first drafts of S38-1 and of issue #49 both said 'the products rows themselves survive'; they do not, so the pre-fix P1-INV-08 exposure was another store's CATALOGUE, not merely its catalogue media. VERIFIED ON THE REAL ENGINE, not inferred from SQLite: tests/Support/Security/bin/verify-category-product-cascade-on-mysql.php, 3 checks 0 failures on MySQL 8.0.46, including information_schema.REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS reporting DELETE_RULE = CASCADE. WHAT P1-INV-08 CLOSED: the cross-tenant path, so a merchant can no longer reach the cascade across a tenant boundary. WHAT IS STILL OPEN: (1) a merchant deleting their OWN category silently destroys every product in it, with no warning and no product count -- the UI says only 'Category delete successfully'; (2) the latent cross-tenant case cannot be closed in the controller, so a foreign product sharing the caller's category keeps its FILES (P1-INV-08's loop predicate) but loses its row and variants, which a regression test now pins deliberately and labels as pinning known-bad behaviour; (3) whether the LIVE schema carries this constraint is unverified and unverifiable from here -- GATE F records 15 tables that live code reads with no migration at all.
